main_text.p: Theologiæ Caluinistarum libros tres, in quibus ceu in tabella quadam, quasi ad oculum plusquam ducentos viginti tres errores Sacramentariorum publicis scriptis, verbis proprijs, & auctorum nominibus indicatis, demonstratur, eos de nullo fere doctrinæ Christianæ articulo recte sentire, addita simul veræ sententiæ assertione, & contrariæ opinionis refutatione. Francofurti 1592. in 4. Dies me deficeret, & charta, si vellem omnia, quæ Martinus Lutherus, Philippus Melanchthon, Franciscus Stanckarus, alijq; scripserunt, ediderunt[?]que contra Caluinistas, & contra Lutheranos Caluinistæ, in medium proferre. Præ manibus omnium sunt certa dogmata, in quibus Lutherani a Caluinistis, seu Sacramentarijs dissentiunt, & Sacramentarij a Lutheranis ingrauissimis fidei dogmatibus. Vin plura ? Non eadem dicunt, tenentque inter se Trinitarij. Sacramentarij Sacramentarios mutuis scriptis damnant, Anabaptistæ Anabaptistas, Lutherani Lutheranos. Et quod manifeste perridiculum est, Caluinus, Melanchthon, Luthe rus a se ipsis in potissimis discordant: nec quid inter ipsos certum fit, nec ipsi sciunt, nec alij capiunt. Ita tenebrarum potestas inter eos conualuit, ue-aiant, negent eodem ipso momento, & dum

page.notes: Page number reads "391"; the last digit is printed in a form close to "r" ("39r"), read here as 1. The left and right scan edges show partial red-brown letters ("pi", "di", "al" and similar) belonging to the neighbouring page or to a stain; they are not transcribed. The hyphenated line end "ve-" / "aiant" is doubtful: the word may read "ue-", "vt" or other, and is given as "ue-aiant". "ediderunt[?]que" is uncertain. The paragraph is taken as continuing from the previous page, since the first line runs on mid-sentence.
